## Nuevo: `lua/pickypen/anchor.lua`

```lua
local M = {}

local SEARCH_WINDOW = 60

-- A snippet with less ink than this matches too much to trust: 'end' or '}'
-- would land on the first one it met rather than the one the comment was about.
local MIN_SNIPPET = 4

-- Everything below reads the file through an `at(lnum)`: the trimmed text of
-- that line, or nil past either end of it. Anchoring never needs more than that.
function M.of_buffer(buf)
  local total = vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf)

  return function(lnum)
    if lnum < 1 or lnum > total then return nil end
    return vim.trim(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, lnum - 1, lnum, false)[1] or '')
  end
end

-- What a comment on this line records so it can be found again later.
function M.snippet(at, lnum) return at(lnum) or '' end

-- Where the comment sits now, or nil if the code it was on is gone.
function M.locate(at, comment)
  local want = vim.trim(comment.snippet or '')
  if want == '' then return at(comment.line) and comment.line or nil end

  if at(comment.line) == want then return comment.line end
  if #want:gsub('%s', '') < MIN_SNIPPET then return nil end

  for delta = 1, SEARCH_WINDOW do
    if at(comment.line - delta) == want then return comment.line - delta end
    if at(comment.line + delta) == want then return comment.line + delta end
  end

  return nil
end

return M
```
